pages.Arthur's Magazine: Arthur's Magazine was an American literary periodical founded in Philadelphia. It was started in 1844 by Timothy Shay Arthur. The magazine published essays, fiction, and commentary aimed at a general audience. It is sometimes confused with later women's magazines of similar name. The publication is distinct from First for Women, a much later title.
pages.First for Women: First for Women is an American women's magazine. It was started in 1989. The magazine covers lifestyle, health, and entertainment topics. It is published more frequently than many literary magazines of the nineteenth century. Its founding year is often used in comparison questions with older periodicals.
Apple Inc. is an American multinational technology company. It designs consumer electronics, software, and online services. The company created the iPhone, which was introduced in 2007. Apple is headquartered in Cupertino, California. Tim Cook has served as chief executive officer since 2011.
pages.iPhone: The iPhone is a line of smartphones designed and marketed by Apple Inc. Apple created the iPhone and announced it in January 2007. The first iPhone was released in the United States in June 2007. It combined a mobile phone, iPod, and internet communicator. Later models added cameras, app stores, and faster processors.
pages.To Kill a Mockingbird: To Kill a Mockingbird is a novel by Harper Lee published in 1960. The story is set in the fictional town of Maycomb, Alabama. A central character is Atticus Finch, a lawyer who defends a Black man accused of a crime. The narrator is Scout Finch, Atticus's daughter. The novel won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction in 1961.
pages.Harper Lee: Nelle Harper Lee was an American novelist. She wrote To Kill a Mockingbird. Lee was born in Monroeville, Alabama, in 1926. She published a second novel, Go Set a Watchman, in 2015. Lee received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2007.
pages.Atticus Finch: Atticus Finch is a fictional character in Harper Lee's novel To Kill a Mockingbird. He is a lawyer in Maycomb, Alabama. Finch is the father of Scout and Jem. He is widely cited as a model of moral integrity in American literature. The character appears in the 1962 film adaptation played by Gregory Peck.
pages.Jane Austen: Jane Austen was an English novelist. She wrote Pride and Prejudice, Emma, and Sense and Sensibility. Austen was born in Steventon, Hampshire, in 1775. She spent most of her life in England. Her novels examine marriage, class, and manners in Georgian society.
pages.Pride and Prejudice: Pride and Prejudice is a novel by Jane Austen, first published in 1813. The book follows Elizabeth Bennet as she deals with issues of manners, upbringing, and marriage. Mr. Darcy is a central character. The novel is among the most famous works in English literature. It has been adapted many times for film and television.
pages.Kenya: Kenya is a country in East Africa. Its capital and largest city is Nairobi. Kenya has a coastline on the Indian Ocean. English and Swahili are official languages. The country is known for wildlife, the Great Rift Valley, and long-distance runners.
pages.Nairobi: Nairobi is the capital and largest city of Kenya. It was founded in 1899 as a railway depot. The city is an economic and diplomatic hub for East Africa. Nairobi National Park lies close to the urban area. The name is derived from a Maasai phrase meaning cool water.
pages.Indian Ocean: The Indian Ocean is the third-largest of the world's oceanic divisions. It is bounded by Africa, Asia, Australia, and the Southern Ocean. East African countries such as Kenya and Tanzania border the Indian Ocean. Important trade routes cross the ocean. Monsoon winds strongly influence its climate.
pages.Sistine Chapel: The Sistine Chapel is a chapel in the Apostolic Palace, the official residence of the pope, in Vatican City. Michelangelo painted the chapel's ceiling between 1508 and 1512. The famous Last Judgment fresco on the altar wall was also painted by Michelangelo later. The chapel is in Vatican City, an independent city-state enclosed by Rome. It is a major destination for visitors to Rome.
pages.Michelangelo: Michelangelo di Lodovico Buonarroti Simoni was an Italian sculptor, painter, and architect of the High Renaissance. He painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel in Vatican City. He also sculpted David and the Pietà. Michelangelo was born in Caprese, Republic of Florence, in 1475. He is often considered one of the greatest artists of all time.
pages.Uranium: Uranium is a chemical element with symbol U and atomic number 92. It is a silvery-grey metal in the actinide series. The element is named after the planet Uranus. Uranium is weakly radioactive. It is used in nuclear power and, in enriched form, in nuclear weapons.
pages.Uranus: Uranus is the seventh planet from the Sun. It was the first planet discovered with a telescope, by William Herschel in 1781. The chemical element uranium was later named after Uranus. Uranus is an ice giant with a pale blue-green color. It rotates on an extreme tilt compared with most planets.
pages.YouTube: YouTube is an online video sharing platform. It was founded in 2005 by Steve Chen, Chad Hurley, and Jawed Karim. Google acquired YouTube in 2006. The site allows users to upload, view, and comment on videos. It is one of the most visited websites in the world.
pages.Google: Google LLC is an American multinational technology company. It is best known for its search engine. Google acquired YouTube in 2006. The company is a subsidiary of Alphabet Inc. Google's other products include Gmail, Google Maps, and Android.
pages.Eiffel Tower: The Eiffel Tower is a wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France. It was designed by Gustave Eiffel's company and opened in 1889. The tower is among the most recognizable structures in the world. Paris is the capital of France. Millions of visitors climb or view the tower each year.
pages.Paris: Paris is the capital and most populous city of France. It is situated on the river Seine. Landmarks include the Eiffel Tower, the Louvre, and Notre-Dame. The city is a global center for art, fashion, and gastronomy. France is a country in Western Europe.
pages.Colorado orogeny: The Colorado orogeny was an episode of mountain building (an orogeny) in Colorado and surrounding areas. The eastern sector extends into the High Plains and is called the Central Plains orogeny. The event affected Proterozoic rocks. Geologists distinguish it from later Laramide deformation. Surrounding areas of the southern Rocky Mountains were also involved.
pages.High Plains (United States): The High Plains are a subregion of the Great Plains. From east to west, the High Plains rise in elevation from around 1,800 to 7,000 ft (550 to 2,130 m). The region covers parts of several U.S. states including Colorado, Kansas, and Nebraska. Agriculture and ranching are important to the local economy. The climate is semi-arid compared with lands farther east.
pages.High Plains: High Plains refers to one of two distinct land regions: the High Plains of the United States and the Highveld-related usage in some other countries. In North American geology, the relevant region is usually the High Plains (United States). Disambiguation is required for precise elevation facts.
pages.Milhouse: Milhouse Mussolini Van Houten is a recurring character in the Fox animated television series The Simpsons voiced by Pamela Hayden and created by Matt Groening. Milhouse was named after U.S. president Richard Nixon, whose middle name was Milhous. He is Bart Simpson's best friend. The character wears glasses and a red sweater. His parents are Kirk and Luann Van Houten.
pages.Nicholas Ray: Nicholas Ray (born Raymond Nicholas Kienzle Jr., August 7, 1911 – June 16, 1979) was an American film director, screenwriter, and actor best known for the 1955 film Rebel Without a Cause. He also directed In a Lonely Place and Johnny Guitar. Ray influenced later generations of filmmakers. He worked in Hollywood during the studio era and after.
pages.Elia Kazan: Elia Kazan was a Greek-American film and theatre director, producer, screenwriter and actor. He directed On the Waterfront and A Streetcar Named Desire. Kazan co-founded the Actors Studio. He worked closely with many major mid-century American actors. His film and stage careers overlapped for decades.
